newsitem.title: CANADA: NBA basketball-VANCOUVER TO HOST 1998 DRAFT.
newsitem.headline: NBA basketball-VANCOUVER TO HOST 1998 DRAFT.

text.p: The Vancouver Grizzlies will host the 1998 NBA draft, the league announced Thursday.
Opened in September 1995, Vancouver's General Motors Place will host the draft on June 24, 1998.

But fans of the second-year Grizzlies have no chance of watching their team select a number one overall pick. The team will not be eligible for the top lottery selection until 1999 under the deal that brought two Canadian teams -- the Grizzlies and the Toronto Raptors -- into the NBA.

"Hosting the NBA draft is a special honour for the city of Vancouver, the Vancouver Grizzlies, Orca Bay and our many fans and season-ticket partners," Grizzlies president Stu Jackson said. "It will be a wonderful opportunity for all of us to showcase British Columbia to the world."
British Columbia Premier Glen Clark and NBA deputy commissioner Russ Granik also participated in the news conference at GM Place announcing the decision.

Last year's draft was in East Rutherford, New Jersey, and this year's will be in Charlotte, North Carolina, on June 25. The 1995 draft was held in Toronto's SkyDome. More than 21,000 fans attended the Toronto draft. Just over 12,000 attended last year in New Jersey.
From 1979-91, the draft was open to the public, but held exclusively in New York. After that, the NBA has moved the draft to different sites each year.
Vancouver also will host the National Hockey League's All-Star Weekend in 1998.
